speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; you are here because your newborn was born three days ago and has been experiencing seizures and lethargy. To begin our investigation, did you notice any unusual odors on the baby's skin, breath, or urine, or any feeding difficulties since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Hypoglycemia.

Based on the clinical picture of a low birth weight infant born to a mother with chorioamnionitis, presenting with lethargy, seizures, hypotonia, irregular respirations, and a tense fontanelle, the immediate priority is to rule out and treat hypoglycemia. The "tense fontanelle" and "sluggish pupils" could also suggest increased intracranial pressure from meningitis, which requires urgent attention.

I need to know the exact glucose level from your blood test results. Also, do you have a lumbar puncture report or any imaging of the head available?

REQUEST TEST: Serum glucose level.
REQUEST IMAGES: Head_ultrasound.
